elements.element: An audit may occur no more than once in any rolling 12-month period.
elements.evidence: The clause permits one inspection “per year,” which may allow two inspections within a rolling 12-month period, such as one late in one calendar year and another early in the next.

elements.element: Vendor must provide at least 30 days' prior written notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires “no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice” to the Company.

elements.element: The audit may be conducted only during Customer's normal business hours.
elements.evidence: Inspection is expressly limited to “the Company's normal business hours.”

elements.element: The audit must be conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: The inspection right is granted to HDI's General Manager, not to an independent auditor.

elements.element: The auditor must be bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no confidentiality obligation applicable to the person conducting the inspection.

elements.element: Vendor must bear the audit costs when any underpayment does not exceed 5%.
elements.evidence: The clause unconditionally requires HDI to bear the fees incurred in connection with the inspection, including where underpayment is 5% or less.

elements.element: Customer may be required to bear audit costs only if underpayment exceeds 5%.
elements.evidence: The clause never shifts inspection fees to the Company; unconditional Vendor payment is more protective than permitting cost shifting above the 5% threshold.

elements.element: The audit right must not permit direct access to Customer systems.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no express prohibition on direct systems access, and a right to inspect records could encompass electronically maintained records.

elements.element: An audit may occur no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: The redline expressly adds “no more than once per year.”

elements.element: Vendor must provide at least 15 days' prior notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires the stronger protection of at least 30 days' prior written notice.

elements.element: Vendor must bear the audit costs when any underpayment does not exceed 10%.
elements.evidence: The clause unconditionally requires HDI to bear the fees incurred in connection with the inspection.

elements.element: Customer may be required to bear audit costs only if underpayment exceeds 10%.
elements.evidence: The clause does not shift inspection fees to the Company under any circumstances, which is more protective than allowing cost shifting only above 10%.

result.reason: The redline minimally adds the frequency cap needed to complete the fallback, while the existing 30-day written-notice and unconditional HDI-cost provisions exceed the fallback protections. It does not satisfy the preferred position because “once per year” is not a rolling 12-month limit, the audit is conducted by HDI's General Manager rather than an independent confidential auditor, and direct access to Customer systems is not expressly prohibited. The drafting preserves the original inspection scope and payment-calculation purpose, though the inherited phrase “may ... have the right” is awkward.
